title: WhatsApp Abandoned Cart Recovery — How to Set It Up
summary: A platform-agnostic setup guide for WhatsApp abandoned cart recovery: the trigger, the message window, and what to send instead of a generic reminder.
body_markdown:
## **How do I set up WhatsApp abandoned cart recovery for my online store?**


At its core it's three pieces: a trigger that fires when a cart is abandoned, a message sent inside a specific time window, and a direct link back to checkout so the customer doesn't have to rebuild their cart from memory. The details depend on which store platform you run, but the shape is the same everywhere.


## **The trigger**


Whatever runs your store needs to notify your messaging tool the moment a cart goes quiet, typically through a webhook or a direct integration, firing after a set period of inactivity at checkout. Commonly that's somewhere between fifteen minutes and an hour, not instantly. Give the customer a real chance to just be mid-purchase, not abandoning. If you're on an ecommerce platform with a WhatsApp integration already, start there. If not, this is the piece that takes the most setup work.


## **The message window that actually matters**


WhatsApp restricts free-form messaging to a 24-hour window after the customer's last interaction. Outside that window, you need an approved message template, not a casual follow-up. That's a platform rule, not a Chatfuel limitation, and it applies no matter which tool sends the message.


Inside that window, send one message with the cart contents and a direct checkout link, and stop there. A second nudge a day later reads as pushy rather than helpful, and repeated follow-ups past the window are what gets numbers blocked, not just ignored.


*Pro-tip: resist the urge to make the recovery message purely a discount. "Your cart's still here" plus a direct link converts customers who were already going to buy. A reflexive discount on every abandoned cart just teaches regular customers to abandon on purpose and wait for the coupon.*


## **Why "connect it to Shopify" isn't the whole answer**


A lot of guides for this topic are really guides for one specific integration, usually Shopify. That's fine if that's your stack, but the actual mechanic (trigger, window, link) works the same whether your store runs on Shopify, WooCommerce, a custom build, or something else entirely. Set it up around the mechanic, not around one platform's specific webhook names, and you won't need to rebuild the flow if you ever migrate your store.
